subject: Dedicated pool saturation impacting HaloAI - remediation & credits
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@haloai.com>, support@haloai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool saturation impacting HaloAI - immediate mitigation and visibility

Hi Rajiv / HaloAI team,

Quick note to confirm we detected a dedicated GPU pool saturation affecting a subset of your production inference queues starting ~08:40 PT this morning. Scope: 3 of your reserved nodes entered sustained 95-100% utilization and requests were queued > 6s for some request classes. We've opened TICKET-7421 for the investigation and assigned an on-call runbook owner.

What we're doing now (immediate):
- Promotional throttling: temporarily limiting concurrency for non-critical routes to preserve capacity for low-latency endpoints (applied 09:00 PT).
- Live migration: initiating a targeted node placement shift to move two of your busiest pods to warm standby capacity (expected ~20–30m).
- Telemetry capture: capturing heap summaries and an incident snapshot (attached) for the post-incident analysis.

Preliminary hypothesis: an autoscaling policy interaction with a bursty multi-tenant background workload caused a transient allocation storm that starved reservation weights for your tenant until the allocator recalculated. We are prioritizing a short-term allocator tweak to stop repeated recirculation.

Impact: degraded tail latency for some long-sequence generation calls; not a total outage. We understand this affected several critical inference flows.

Asking you: can you share the highest-priority routes we should pin during the mitigation window (route names or example request IDs)? Also please confirm any maintenance blackout windows we should avoid.

I'll send a remediation update in ~30 minutes and a follow-up with a postmortem once we complete the root-cause analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this matters.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@haloai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 09:21:38 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation impacting HaloAI - immediate mitigation and visibility

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the quick heads up.

We saw increased 95th/99th latency on our realtime inference route (route: /v1/infer/realtime) starting ~08:35. A few customers reported timeouts.

Priority routes: /v1/infer/realtime (high), /v1/infer/batch (medium). Please avoid any reboots or migrations on nodes servicing reprocessing jobs between 10:00–11:30 PT, we have a scheduled batch window then.

Two asks:
1) Any ETA on when tail latency will return to SLOs?
2) Please confirm whether we should expect a billing credit for the degraded experience and how that will be calculated — we track inference success rates internally and will share a short impact matrix.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Kumar
Head of Platform, HaloAI
rajiv@haloai.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@haloai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation impacting HaloAI - immediate mitigation and visibility

Thanks Rajiv — quick update and concrete next steps.

Current status (10:05 PT):
- Migration + allocator tweak completed at 09:38 PT. Two busiest pods moved to warm standby and the allocator weighting change prevented further recirculation.
- Observed tail latency dropped from peak 12s -> 1.2s for /v1/infer/realtime; p95 back within SLO, p99 improving.
- No node reboots performed; we avoided interrupting scheduled batch window per your note.

Root-cause (high level):
- The autoscaler had an interaction with a background multi-tenant backfill task that triggered simultaneous allocation attempts. The allocator's fairness policy briefly deprioritized reserved weights for some tenants during the recalc window.
- Contributing factor: a recent autoscaler tuning change that made grow operations faster but did not extend reservation lockouts during recalc.

Short-term fixes applied (done):
1) allocator fair-weight guard (hotfix) — prevents reservation demotion during recalc (deployed 09:25 PT).
2) conservative autoscaler roll-back for the affected flavor (reverted 09:30 PT).
3) emergency throttles (route-level) — applied 09:00–09:35 for non-critical routes to stabilize headroom.

Planned next steps (post-incident):
- Full RCA and timeline by 2028-05-11 16:00 PT (we'll share the doc link).
- Permanent allocator fixes and an autoscaler regression test to prevent recurrence.
- Proposal for a goodwill credit: a pro-rated usage credit for the minutes where p99 exceeded your SLO threshold (I will loop in Finance & Sales for precise calculation).

We attached the captured heap summary and snapshot. The drive link above contains a live runbook and a short traffic replay you can use to validate.

Ben / Dev / Marissa — FYI: HaloAI asked about expected credit calculation method and confirmation of final remediation timeline. Please coordinate with Finance & Solutions.

— Naomi

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@haloai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: HaloAI dedicated pool saturation (RCA, fixes, credits)

Rajiv / HaloAI team —

Apologies again for the disruption last week. Attached below is a concise post-incident summary and the concrete actions we're taking. If you'd like a full deep-dive call we can schedule with Eng + Product.

Summary (what happened):
- Time window: 2028-05-04 08:35–09:40 PT.
- Impact: transient tail latency increases for heavy-sequence generation calls; p99 peaked ~12s for /v1/infer/realtime. No data loss.
- Root cause: autoscaler tuning change + allocation recalc fairness edge case allowed a backfill task to temporarily preempt reserved weights.

What we fixed (already deployed):
- Allocator fair-weight guard (permanent): prevents reservation demotion during recalc windows.
- Autoscaler rollback for affected flavor + added a pre-deploy regression test that replays tenant reservation scenarios.
- Improved telemetry alert: new signal for rapid recirculation events and a circuit breaker that will stop concurrent growth if reservation assignment is below threshold.

Action items and ETA:
- Engineering: full postmortem doc with timeline and diffs — 2028-05-13 EOD.
- Product/Reliability: add a canary that simulates your realtime traffic shape — 2028-05-20.
- Billing: proposing a one-time credit equivalent to 7.5% of your billed usage for the impacted hour (draft calculation attached). We will finalize this by 2028-05-15.

Requested from HaloAI: please review the short impact matrix you mentioned so we can align the credit calculation and confirm whether you'd like the canary to run against a staging mirror.

Again — we take this seriously. If you prefer a synchronous review with our SRE + Product, propose a few slots next week and we'll set it up.

Thanks for the partnership,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
